prerequisites: Prior knowledge in Technical and Applied Mechanics

learning_outcomes.text: Consolidate knowledge in the field of Technical and Applied Mechanics and understand the relationship between Technical Mechanics and other general technical disciplines.
Assimilate basic knowledge applicable in the development of other specialized disciplines.
Develop the ability to solve fundamental elementary problems in mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Equilibrium of a free material point and subject to constraints. Types of constraints.
Moment of a force with respect to a point. Moment of a force with respect to an axis. Couples of forces.
Reduction of a system of forces, elements of the reduction wrench. Central axis. Analytical reduction.
Equilibrium of a body and systems of bodies. Equilibrium of a cable.
Kinematics of a material point. Study of motion in different coordinate systems.
Kinematics of a rigid body. Properties of velocity and acceleration distributions.
Particular motions of a rigid body: translational motion, rotation about a fixed axis, roto-translational motion, planar and with a fixed point.
Kinematics of relative motion. Composition of motions.
Equilibrium of a material point. Moment of a force with respect to a point and an axis.
Centers of gravity for bars, plates, bodies.
Kinematics of a material point. Kinematic study in different coordinate systems.
Particular motions of a rigid body.
Kinematics of relative motion of a material point.
assessment_rules: The overall grade is determined by a written exam for the course (2/3 weight) and a written exam for applied activities (1/3 weight). A minimum grade of 5 is required for each subject and for ongoing activity during the semester to pass the discipline.
